correctness.rationale: Taking the CDF power gives the location change with the stated minus sign and mass exp(-c_n). For a scaled negative excursion t, the ratio of the two CDFs gives the exact conditional survival exp[-c_n*expm1(t^p/c_n)]. The single exponential coupling realizes these conditional laws (not the original nested maxima); c*log(1+E/c) has positive derivative for E>0 and tends to E. On either branch put v=|x|^p/sigma. The density is proportional to v^k y exp(-y), where y=c_n exp(v) on the negative branch and y=c_n exp(-v) on the positive branch. The log scores k/v+1-y and k/v+y-1 both strictly decrease from positive infinity and each crosses zero once. The density vanishes at zero and at both tails, so these are strict distinct local maxima at every n. At the negative root t=c_n*v solves t exp(t/c_n)=k+t/c_n, giving t=k+O(1/c_n) and y=c_n+k+O(1/c_n); substituting preserves the exp(-k) height factor. At the positive root v=L-log(1-k/v), L=log c_n, which gives v=L+k/L+O(L^-2) and y tending to 1. Restoring units gives the two stated positions and heights; their ratio forces eventual unique positive global dominance. The ordinary unconditioned normalization follows by expanding the inverse signed power of b_n+sigma*G on its eventually positive branch. Independent high-precision finite checks corroborated the two location and height scales.
residual_risks: Requires independent samples and fixed p>1, mu and sigma>0. The rare conditioned Weibull law is not the law of typical maxima. Positive global dominance is eventually, not universally, asserted.

originality.rationale: The signed-power Gumbel family, underlying mode equation and closure from max-stability are prior ingredients. The assessed addition is the combined rare conditional law and quantitative description of both peaks across block sizes. Comparison with the exact underlying model and the related published block-maxima limit found no covering statement of the conditional boundary layer together with the sharp peak asymptotics. Conditioning and stationary-point analysis are standard methods, not asserted as new.
residual_risks: Generic conditional excess results and unindexed transformed-extreme analyses may contain individual ingredients. The checked material supports only a bounded originality judgment for the combined, specifically parameterized modal and conditional result.

value.rationale: Bimodality is a defining feature of the model, so comparing its persistence under the standard block-maximum operation with the actual branch mass is natural. A zero-density valley preserves two strict local modes while the secondary peak and branch probability collapse on explicit different scales. The conditional law describes the fluctuations within that shrinking branch and the peak constants distinguish this from merely restating closure or the ordinary Gumbel limit.
residual_risks: No inference about observed multimodality for dependent or parameter-varying blocks, and no statistical estimation claims.
